newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: BP sees its Venezuelan oil output rising rapidly.
newsitem.headline: BP sees its Venezuelan oil output rising rapidly.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc sees its Venezuelan oil output rising to 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of 1998, double its previous production forecasts, Venezuela's state news agency Venpres quoted the company as saying on Sunday.
BP Venezuela's Anthony Hayward said new seismic exploration techniques had raised the production forecast of the Pedernales field in the eastern Delta Amacuro province.
Output would reach 75,000 bpd by the beginning of next year from a current flow of 20,000 bpd, Venpres reported.

BP operates the Pedernales field for state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) under an operating agreement and receives a fixed fee for every barrel produced. Hayward said the field was abandoned due to low production in 1960, but was revived in 1980 by PDVSA subsidiary Lagoven and was assigned to BP in a "marginal" fields licensing round. PDVSA plans to award another 20 such fields in May under a third licensing round in which BP is one of 259 companies participating.
